questions.question: Which sorting algorithm guarantees O(n log n) even in the WORST case, unlike Quick Sort?
questions.solutionApproach: Merge Sort and Heap Sort both guarantee Θ(n log n) worst case; Quick Sort's worst case is O(n²).

questions.question: What is the minimum number of comparisons needed to sort 4 elements (comparison-based, worst case)?
Array [5,1,4,2,8]. How many passes of Bubble Sort (with early-exit optimization) are needed to fully sort it?
questions.solutionApproach: Pass1: 5,1,4,2,8→1,4,2,5,8 (swaps happened). Pass2: 1,4,2,5,8→1,2,4,5,8 (swap happened). Pass3: no swaps needed, array already sorted → early exit. 3 passes total (2 with swaps + 1 confirming pass).
questions.answer: 3 passes (2 active + 1 confirmation pass with no swaps)

questions.question: You have an array of n integers, each guaranteed to be in range [0, 99]. What's the fastest way to sort it, and what complexity?
questions.solutionApproach: Range is bounded and small (constant, independent of n) — use Counting Sort. O(n+k) = O(n+100) = O(n), linear time, beating the Ω(n log n) comparison-sort bound since we're not comparison-based.
questions.answer: Counting Sort, O(n) — bounded range enables linear-time non-comparison sorting.
